Count the time people must stay available

By v/hNovember 21, 2026Note

Originally shared
on LinkedIn

View the post ↗← All journal entries

A device can do the work and still keep you waiting beside it.

Imagine a utility that pauses halfway through a job to ask for a choice it could have collected at the start. Answering takes a moment, but the owner has to keep track of when to return.

We would want the starting controls to collect foreseeable choices. A local agent should use the available inputs to plan the job before acting. If new conditions require help, the device should pause safely and make the unfinished state clear.

When a task can safely run without supervision, the person should be free to get on with something else. A development check should record how long they must remain available, alongside how long the device takes to finish.

Our first utility is in development. The example describes a proposed design requirement.

Which everyday device keeps you waiting for a decision you could have made at the start?
